title: App Development in San Francisco, CA | 22 Signals
description: App development for San Francisco companies: iOS, Android and web apps, SaaS products and companion apps for hardware, from first version to app store launch.
h1: App development for San Francisco products that need to ship
intro: We build iOS, Android and web apps for San Francisco companies: SaaS products, customer apps, companion apps for connected hardware and internal tools. One accountable lead takes the app from scope to app store launch and support, with payments, APIs, AI features and California privacy requirements handled from the first sprint.

sections.h: Your engineers are busy with the core product
p: In the Bay Area the problem is rarely a lack of engineering talent. It is that your engineers are fully booked on the core platform, and the mobile app, the customer portal or the new product line keeps slipping a quarter. Hiring a mobile team for one app is slow and expensive in this market, and contractors found through a marketplace often leave without documentation.

We take on the app as a defined project with a written scope and dates. Your team keeps ownership of the architecture decisions and the code. We do the building, and hand it back in a state your engineers would have been happy to write.

Some clients have the opposite problem: a professional services firm or a clinic group with no engineers at all, and an idea for an app their customers keep asking for. The app development San Francisco firms like these need starts with a smaller first release, clear costs to run it, and someone who will keep it working after launch.

sections.h: Privacy rules that apply to California apps
p: California's Online Privacy Protection Act requires apps that collect personal information from California residents to post a privacy policy. The California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the CPRA, adds rights to access and delete data. Health apps carry more weight: the Confidentiality of Medical Information Act can apply to businesses that offer software designed to maintain medical information. The app stores add their own privacy labels and data-use questions.
We build data maps as we go, so your privacy policy, store labels and deletion process describe what the app really does. Your counsel signs off on the wording.

sections.h: How a build runs: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we run a short discovery with product, design and engineering, and with a few real users if you can introduce them. Plan: user flows, technical approach, scope for the first release and a written launch date. Build: two-week sprints, a test build in your hands after each one, and automated tests from the start. Grow: launch, crash and usage monitoring, then the next release based on what users actually do.

We are developing an AI commentary product for live esports, which has to follow fast-moving matches and respond in near real time. It is still in development, and we say so. The work behind it, from streaming data to model latency and testing, is the same work that goes into AI features for San Francisco apps.

faqs.q: Native or cross-platform for our app?
faqs.a: It depends on what the app does. Cross-platform with React Native or Flutter suits most business and consumer apps and saves building twice. Native Swift and Kotlin suit apps with heavy device features, such as Bluetooth hardware pairing, camera work or complex animation. We recommend one after the discovery and explain the trade-off.

faqs.q: Do you build apps for hardware companies?
faqs.a: Yes. Companion apps for connected devices are common in the Bay Area. We build pairing flows, device dashboards, firmware update screens and the cloud services behind them, working with your firmware team's specifications. Bluetooth work needs real devices, so we agree early how test hardware reaches our developers.

We agree that in writing at the start, covering the code, developer accounts and cloud resources, and you always have access to what we build and run for you. We document the architecture and the release process so your engineers can take over at any point, and we never hold accounts or credentials hostage.

faqs.q: Can you add AI features to our existing app?
faqs.a: Yes. We add search, summaries, assistants and recommendations to existing apps, using your data and the model provider that fits your terms. Before release we test each feature against real examples and set limits on what it can do, so it fails safely rather than confidently.

faqs.q: Do you work with San Francisco app clients in person?
faqs.a: We work remotely from London with teams across four regions and keep sprint calls in the Pacific morning. App development runs well remotely because builds, test versions and tickets are shared online. For design sprints or user testing in the Bay Area, we plan a visit when the project needs it.

faqs.q: How do you handle California privacy rules in an app?
faqs.a: We build a data map as the app grows, listing what is collected, why and where it goes. That feeds your privacy policy under California law, the app store privacy labels and the in-app deletion flow. Health apps get extra review because of medical privacy law. Your counsel approves the final wording.

faqs.q: How much does app development cost in San Francisco?
faqs.a: It depends on platforms, screens, integrations, AI features and support after launch. We do not publish prices because two apps with the same screen count can differ a lot in effort. After a 15-minute call and a short discovery, we give you a written scope and cost before anything is built.
